summary:
Pinned Arch v7.2.11-arch1 source permits a possible targeted ACTIVE-namespace retirement witness through nsfs file handles. Its lookup obtains a namespace by identity only while its active-reference state permits reopening. Namespace-file opening can reactivate a subtree still retained by other reference classes; active retirement is not universal reference or old-reader absence. Source availability and matching version text do not attest the deployed binary/configuration or actual syscall capability.

Foreign namespace resolution requires the initial PID namespace plus CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace. Merely owning the target user namespace or being UID0 inside another container is insufficient. Critically, the VFS decoder turns decode errors other than ENOMEM, including permission failures, into ESTALE. An ordinary UID1000 outside observer can therefore see ESTALE for an ALIVE unauthorized namespace. Neither a valid-looking handle nor a stale errno alone establishes retirement.

A candidate must authenticate exact original/boot/namespace type/inode/opaque handle and demonstrate live positive reopening under the SAME fully authorized resolver context before releasing old-store access. Later queries require unchanged authority and identity. Temporary capture/reopen target FDs must close; the resolver anchor must not retain the target namespace. A separately owned external target-namespace-FD holder must keep reopening successful after worker retirement; only after that holder closes may an authenticated stale result count. Unexpected errors, malformed or mismatched handles, unsupported ABI, changed credentials/namespaces or uncertain persistence remain Unknown, without automatic retry or wider acceptance.

This witness still needs closed source-owned NO namespace-FD AND NO selected-old-file/mount-FD export, actual writer/partial-role retirement and complete lease ordering. Weak/passive references and namespace types have different lifetimes. A kernel worker-group-empty receipt is another scoped fact, not a substitute. Reusing the existing authenticated Root host actor is a plausible resolver route, requiring separately reviewed finite source and genuine deployed positive/retained-reference/retired controls; no new token/App or host privilege change follows from source research.

At the source-research checkpoint no namespace-handle syscall/probe had been selected or performed for this route, and operational copy remained refused. A separately prepared fixture later obtained independent source approval with pure controls; its Root executor, hard-parent placement, wait provenance and genuine deployed behavior still required qualification. Source approval supplies none of those runtime facts. Root source findings and Home's protocol correction are public at https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4516#issuecomment-6409512043 and https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4516#issuecomment-6409599554. Preserve this source-versus-capability boundary through any later qualification. Raw source caches, host facts, logs and runtime assets are excluded from Atlas.
title: Namespace handle staleness requires authenticated active-reference semantics
